name: disk_budget_absolute_20261109
comment: LQ-20261107-1638 (2026-11-09). Operator: 'a new 2TB drive is going in this week; hygiene must NOT
relax because there is more space — cache and scratch must not just grow.' Measured before the change:
the standing lane planned 19.65 GiB of rule T and applied 0.78 GiB, ~/.cache/agent-tmp held 91.3 GiB
across 592 entries with 0 candidates, and the monitor bands on used% only — so the same 420 GB reads
95% on this 468 GB disk and 21% on the 2 TB one arriving this week.
Pins: the operator's D16 numbers (keep 24 h, cap 10 GB) exist in config/disk_hygiene_rules.json, not
only in apply_scratch_cap(); every budget root and every ENABLED cache root names a positive absolute
byte cap and the rule that feeds it; a root over cap is reclaimed oldest-first (fingerprint.activity or
the rule-C newest mtime), only as far as the cap needs, and a candidate that must stay is re-excluded
with budget_over_cap_kept, never dropped; a protected floor above the cap is reported and ESCALATED,
never crossed; held entries past max_item_age_days are counted with the reason that holds them; the
monitor measures each root from the lane that owns it and reports unmeasured (band None) rather than 0;
growth is GiB/day over the sample window with min_samples, so a quiet mount still alerts.
Synthetic rows and configs only; no host tree is walked and nothing is deleted.
